classification.difficultyReason: Select and combine age groups before calculating percentages using the supplied total, then recognise that the table omits ages 0–5.

inlines.text: Data on the ages of male inhabitants of the Maldives in 2001 are presented in the table below. The total number of males is 226 634.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many male inhabitants of the Maldives are aged between 10 and 14?

answer.worked: The entry for the 10–14 years age group is 41 089 males.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of males are aged under 25? Give your answer to the nearest per cent.

answer.worked:
Using the listed age groups under 25:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number under 25}&=30\,813+41\,089+33\,266+23\,514\\\text{Number under 25}&=128\,682\\\text{Percentage under 25}&=\frac{128\,682}{226\,634}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage under 25}&\approx57\%\end{align*}$$
The percentage uses the data as given; part d identifies the missing age group.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of males are aged between 15 and 24? Give your answer to the nearest per cent.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Number aged 15–24}&=33\,266+23\,514\\\text{Number aged 15–24}&=56\,780\\\text{Percentage aged 15–24}&=\frac{56\,780}{226\,634}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage aged 15–24}&\approx25\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is wrong with the given data?

answer.short: There is no entry for the 0–5 years age group.
answer.worked: The first age group is 6–9 years, so males aged 0–5 years are omitted.

inlines.text: Data has been collected on the nationalities of some of the visitors to certain island resorts. The table below gives the available data. In the table, (A) indicates that the country is in Asia, (E) indicates that the country is in Europe and (O) indicates that the country is neither in Asia nor in Europe.
Number of visitors (tens of thousands per year)
Use the table above to answer the following questions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the total number of visitors from Japan?

answer.worked:
$$23\times10\,000=230\,000$$
230 000 visitors per year.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the total number of visitors from Asia?

answer.worked:
The countries marked (A) are Japan, Singapore and Korea.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Asian visitors}&=(23+5+5)\times10\,000\\\text{Asian visitors}&=330\,000\end{align*}$$
330 000 visitors per year.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of the total number of visitors came from Europe? Give your answer to the nearest per cent.

answer.short:
75%.

Divide the total for countries marked (E) by the total for all countries, then multiply by 100.
answer.worked:
Using the table's units of tens of thousands:
$$\begin{align*}\text{European total}&=6+3.5+14+45+23+12\\\text{European total}&=103.5\\\text{Overall total}&=103.5+(23+5+5)+(0.5+1+0.25)\\\text{Overall total}&=138.25\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{European percentage}&=\frac{103.5}{138.25}\times100\%\\\text{European percentage}&=\frac{41\,400}{553}\%\\\text{European percentage}&\approx75\%\quad\text{(nearest per cent)}\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Aggregate match results into a summary table, compare totals and express a win count as a percentage.

inlines.text: The table below gives the results of a tennis tournament between Rishi, Bryce, Gerald and John.
Complete the following summary table using the information given above.

answer.worked:
Count each player's match wins and losses, then total their sets won and the opponents' sets in those matches.

Rishi: 2 wins, 1 loss; sets won $0+3+3=6$, sets lost $3+2+2=7$.

Bryce: 3 wins, 0 losses; sets won $3+3+3=9$, sets lost $0+1+0=1$.

Gerald: 1 win, 2 losses; sets won $2+1+3=6$, sets lost $3+3+2=8$.

John: 0 wins, 3 losses; sets won $2+0+2=4$, sets lost $3+3+3=9$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Who won the most matches?

answer.worked: Bryce won 3 matches, more than Rishi (2), Gerald (1) or John (0).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Who played the most sets?

answer.worked: Total sets played are Rishi: $6+7=13$; Bryce: $9+1=10$; Gerald: $6+8=14$; John: $4+9=13$. Gerald played the most sets, 14.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What percentage of the matches Gerald played did he win?

answer.worked:
Gerald won 1 of his 3 matches.
$$\frac{1}{3}\times100\%=33\frac{1}{3}\%$$

Adrian cannot also be 4th. Therefore Jonathon’s correct prediction must be Rory 3rd.

Jonathon cannot also be 2nd. Therefore Adrian’s correct prediction must be Adrian 1st.

inlines.text: The table below shows the numbers of students enrolled in the various faculties of a university. There is a total of 2250 students.

children.label: i
children.prompt: How many of the students are not enrolled in Arts?

answer.worked:
$$2250-815=1435$$
1435 students are not enrolled in Arts.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What percentage of students are studying Science?

children.label: b
children.prompt: Display the data using:

children.label: i
children.prompt: a column graph

answer.worked: Use a vertical scale from 0 to 900 students, with major intervals of 200 students. Draw equal-width columns with heights 225, 125, 54, 815, 620 and 411 for Science, Medicine, Law, Arts, Commerce and Engineering respectively. Include a title and label both axes.

spec.description: Six equal-width unfilled columns with labelled axes and a numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: Science 225; Medicine 125; Law 54; Arts 815; Commerce 620; Engineering 411.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: a divided bar chart

answer.short: See the divided bar chart. Segment lengths are proportional to the faculty counts.
answer.worked:
Use an overall bar length of 10 cm. For each faculty, segment length is its student count divided by 2250, multiplied by 10 cm.
$$\begin{align*}L_{\text{Science}}&=\frac{225}{2250}\times10=1\text{ cm}\\L_{\text{Medicine}}&=\frac{125}{2250}\times10=\frac59\text{ cm}\\L_{\text{Law}}&=\frac{54}{2250}\times10=0.24\text{ cm}\\L_{\text{Arts}}&=\frac{815}{2250}\times10=\frac{163}{45}\text{ cm}\\L_{\text{Commerce}}&=\frac{620}{2250}\times10=\frac{124}{45}\text{ cm}\\L_{\text{Engineering}}&=\frac{411}{2250}\times10=\frac{137}{75}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Label the six segments. Percentages shown on the chart are rounded to one decimal place where necessary.

spec.description: One rectangle divided into six exact proportional segments, individually identified with labels or leaders.
spec.mathematics: Cumulative boundaries on a 10 cm bar: 0, 1, 14/9, 404/225, 1219/225, 613/75, 10.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: a pie chart

answer.short: See the pie chart. Sector angles, in table order: $36^\circ$, $20^\circ$, $8.64^\circ$, $130.4^\circ$, $99.2^\circ$, $65.76^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Calculate each sector angle as its fraction of the total multiplied by $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta_{\text{Science}}&=\frac{225}{2250}\times360^\circ=36^\circ\\\theta_{\text{Medicine}}&=\frac{125}{2250}\times360^\circ=20^\circ\\\theta_{\text{Law}}&=\frac{54}{2250}\times360^\circ=8.64^\circ\\\theta_{\text{Arts}}&=\frac{815}{2250}\times360^\circ=130.4^\circ\\\theta_{\text{Commerce}}&=\frac{620}{2250}\times360^\circ=99.2^\circ\\\theta_{\text{Engineering}}&=\frac{411}{2250}\times360^\circ=65.76^\circ\end{align*}$$
The angles total $360^\circ$. Draw the sectors using a protractor and label each faculty.

content.prompt: The graph below shows the journey of two friends Algie and Bertie from the Post Office at Walton.

spec.description: Two distance–time journeys with labelled axes, ticks and dashed grid at 10-unit intervals. Bertie is blue; Algie is black.
spec.mathematics: Bertie: (0,0), (20,20), (30,20), (50,50). Algie: straight segment from (10,0) to (40,50). Both axes range from 0 to 50.
spec.answerVisibility: All source journey lines and names are permanent givens; no calculated speeds or intersection annotation are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the average speed in km/h of Bertie for:

children.label: i
children.prompt: the first 20 minutes of his journey?

answer.worked:
Bertie travels $20\text{ km}$ in $20\text{ minutes}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time taken}&=\frac{20}{60}\text{ h}=\frac13\text{ h}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{20}{1/3}\\\text{Average speed}&=60\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the last 20 minutes of his journey?

answer.worked:
The last 20 minutes run from minute 30 to minute 50.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance travelled}&=50-20=30\text{ km}\\\text{Time taken}&=\frac{20}{60}\text{ h}=\frac13\text{ h}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{30}{1/3}\\\text{Average speed}&=90\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: When and where does Bertie stop and for how long?

answer.short: From 20 to 30 minutes after starting, 20 km from Walton, for 10 minutes.
answer.worked:
Bertie's graph is horizontal at $20\text{ km}$ from minute 20 to minute 30, so he is stationary there.
$$\text{Stopping time}=30-20=10\text{ minutes}.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is Algie’s average speed in km/h?

answer.worked:
Algie travels $50\text{ km}$ from minute 10 to minute 40.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time taken}&=40-10=30\text{ minutes}\\\text{Time taken}&=\frac{30}{60}\text{ h}=\frac12\text{ h}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{50}{1/2}\\\text{Average speed}&=100\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: When and where does Algie pass Bertie?

answer.short: 22 minutes after Bertie starts, 20 km from Walton.
answer.worked: Read the intersection of Algie's rising line and Bertie's horizontal segment. It is at approximately $(22,20)$: 22 minutes after Bertie starts and 20 km from Walton.

content.prompt: The towns of Aral and Smolyvar are 40 km apart. The graphs show the journeys of Ivan and Petruska. Ivan starts from Smolyvar, travels to Aral and returns. Petruska travels from Aral to Smolyvar. They use the same route.

spec.description: Two directly labelled journeys with dashed grid lines and the source's visible fractional intersection guides. Width increased to accommodate fractional tick labels.
spec.mathematics: Ivan: (0,0), (20,40), (30,40), (60,0). Petruska: (0,40), (20,20), (30,20), (40,0). Intersection: (40/3,80/3). Horizontal units are minutes; vertical units are kilometres.
spec.answerVisibility: All plotted journeys and fractional guides are printed givens and remain visible in the question edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the total distance travelled by Ivan?

answer.worked:
Ivan travels 40 km to Aral and 40 km back.
$$\text{Total distance}=40+40=80\text{ km}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is Petruska’s average speed in km/h for the whole journey?

answer.worked:
Petruska travels 40 km in 40 minutes, including her stop.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total time}&=\frac{40}{60}\text{ h}\\\text{Total time}&=\frac{2}{3}\text{ h}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{40}{2/3}\\\text{Average speed}&=60\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long does Ivan take to complete his journey?

answer.worked: Ivan’s graph returns to 0 km from Smolyvar at 60 minutes. His whole journey takes 60 minutes.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is Ivan’s average speed in km/h for the whole journey?

answer.worked:
Ivan travels 80 km in 60 minutes, including his stop.
$$\text{Total time}=\frac{60}{60}=1\text{ h}.$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{80}{1}\\\text{Average speed}&=80\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: How long does Ivan stay in Aral?

answer.worked:
Ivan’s graph is horizontal at 40 km from 20 to 30 minutes.
$$\text{Time in Aral}=30-20=10\text{ minutes}.$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: When and where does Ivan pass Petruska?

answer.worked: The journeys intersect where Ivan passes Petruska. Reading the printed dashed guides gives a time of $13\frac{1}{3}$ minutes and a distance of $26\frac{2}{3}\text{ km}$ from Smolyvar.

entries.description: A pie chart (sector graph) is a circle that is divided into sectors by radii. The sectors are usually shaded in different colours. A pie chart is more complicated than a bar chart to construct, but gives an impression of the proportion of the whole represented by each category of data.

entries.description:
Consider the following simple example with only two categories of data.
Alex is awake for 16 hours and asleep for 8 hours. There are only two sectors required. Alex is asleep for \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the day. We draw a sector with angle \(\frac{1}{3}\times360^\circ=120^\circ\) to represent the part of the day Alex is asleep. The other sector represents the part of the day when he is awake. The angle for this sector is \(\frac{2}{3}\times360^\circ=240^\circ\).
